newsitem.title: FRANCE: New French report recommends fixing clocks.
newsitem.headline: New French report recommends fixing clocks.

text.p: France took a step closer to setting its clocks at different times from its European Union neighbours on Thursday when a new parliamentary report recommended abandoning a twice-yearly change of clocks.
Francois Michel Gonnot, a centre-right member of the National Assembly who drafted the report for Prime Minister Alain Juppe, said France would consult its EU partners first.
The report, matching the conclusions of a Senate inquiry earlier this month, recommended that France fix its clocks at GMT plus one hour, currently winter time in most EU nations.

France and its EU neighbours now put clocks forward an hour in summer under a policy aimed at saving energy and creating long summer evenings. Clocks in the EU go back to winter time on Saturday, including in France.

"The decision by France to return to a fixed time depends on an EU decision," Gonnot said. He added France would risk a serious row if it tried to change its time before 1998, when an EU directive on time comes up for review.
Official French reports argue that energy savings are minimal in summer time and that farmers, truck drivers and children getting up early to go to school would benefit from lighter mornings.
Polls show few French people like the present system.

President Jacques Chirac has broken with his EU partners in the past, notably by staging nuclear tests in the south Pacific and by delaying a seven-nation plan to open land borders. At the same time, France has sought to stay in step with Germany over plans for a single currency from 1999.
